policy.note: Figure 2: Learns embodiment-agnostic skill representations through inverse and forward skill dynamics, then conditions robot diffusion policies on skills extracted from human videos.

policy.alt: DROC policy architecture and execution flow
policy.note: Figure 1: Distills reusable knowledge from online language corrections and retrieves past visual / textual experiences to correct robot plans and skill parameters.

policy.alt: ARCHITECT policy architecture and execution flow
policy.note: PDF page 2, Figure 1: Uses human language feedback and execution traces to synthesize modular robot programs and retain corrected behaviors in a reusable skill library.

policy.alt: Lifelong Robot Library Learning (LRLL) policy architecture and execution flow
policy.note: Figure 2: Alternates human-guided exploration with skill abstraction to compress successful experiences into a growing composable robot-program library.

policy.alt: LYRA policy architecture and execution flow
policy.note: PDF page 3, Figure 2: Distills human feedback into modular reusable skills and retrieves skill / example memory to generate ultra-long-horizon robot programs.

policy.alt: Teach-and-Grow Learning (TGL) policy architecture and execution flow
policy.note: Figure 2: Turns a few successful demonstrations into closed-loop Skill Blocks, then expands a verified skill library and experience memory from execution.

policy.alt: REFLECT policy architecture and execution flow
policy.note: Figure 2: Summarizes multisensory robot experience into structured events, explains execution failures and supplies those explanations to a correction planner.

policy.alt: KnowNo policy architecture and execution flow
policy.note: Figure 1: Calibrates a language planner with conformal prediction so it requests human clarification when multiple next actions remain plausible.

policy.alt: RACER policy architecture and execution flow
policy.note: Figure 3: A vision-language supervisor issues rich corrective instructions to a visuomotor actor trained with failure-recovery trajectories.

policy.alt: Language Model Predictive Control (LMPC) policy architecture and execution flow
policy.note: Figure 3: Learns to predict future human–robot teaching interactions, then searches imagined interaction rollouts to choose code responses that require fewer corrections.

policy.alt: CorrectVLA policy architecture and execution flow
policy.note: Figure 2: Converts one task-level language correction into temporally scoped additive action adjustments while preserving the underlying VLA weights.

policy.credit: Attributed Waypoints and Demonstration Augmentation (AWDA) authors
policy.alt: Attributed Waypoints and Demonstration Augmentation (AWDA) policy architecture and execution flow
policy.note: Figure 3: Separates demonstration-conditioned task inference from execution by predicting attributed waypoints that hand-crafted motor primitives can realize.

policy.alt: ORION policy architecture and execution flow
policy.note: Figure 3: Extracts open-world object-graph plans from a single human video and grounds object-centric interaction geometry to execute the task in a new scene.

policy.alt: PhysCaP policy architecture and execution flow
policy.note: Figure 2: Uses targeted physical interaction to estimate latent properties such as mass and stiffness before synthesizing a robot-control program.

policy.alt: Achievement-Grounded Memory (AGM) policy architecture and execution flow
policy.note: PDF page 3, Figure 1: Advances a task-memory pointer only after verifying physical achievement, preventing attempted actions from being stored as completed progress.

policy.alt: Steerable Policies policy architecture and execution flow
policy.note: Figure 3: Trains VLAs to follow commands at task, subtask, motion and image-coordinate levels, then controls them with a learned reasoner or a prompted VLM.

policy.alt: Guava-4B policy architecture and execution flow
policy.note: Figure 1: Distills physically validated frontier-model interaction traces into a compact tool-using manipulation agent, with perturbation branches teaching recovery.

policy.alt: Pigey / Physical Agency policy architecture and execution flow
policy.note: PDF page 5, Figure 2: Routes subgoals through complementary frozen VLA and geometric-planning backends, verifying outcomes and recovering through a closed physical-agent loop.

policy.alt: MALMM policy architecture and execution flow
policy.note: Figure 2: Coordinates separate planner, coder and supervisor agents to generate manipulation programs and recover from failures using observations after each step.

policy.alt: PRoC3S policy architecture and execution flow
policy.note: Figure 2: Prompts an LLM to synthesize programs with open continuous parameters, then solves their geometric / kinematic constraints and replans infeasible specifications.

policy.alt: In-Context Abstraction Learning (ICAL) policy architecture and execution flow
policy.note: PDF page 4, Figure 1 top panel: noisy demonstrations become revised multimodal examples through abstraction, human feedback and memory.

policy.alt: EmbodiSkill policy architecture and execution flow
policy.note: Figure 2: Distinguishes faulty skill content from failures to follow valid guidance, then makes targeted revisions to an external procedural skill.

policy.alt: Uni-Skill (SkillFolder) policy architecture and execution flow
policy.note: Figure 3: Uses a hierarchical skill-video repository to retrieve examples, implement missing skills and extend a robot planner beyond a fixed initial skill library.

policy.alt: Act-Observe-Rewrite (AOR) policy architecture and execution flow
policy.note: PDF page 5, Figure 1: Rewrites the full Python controller between episodes using multimodal failure evidence, while the generated controller executes the next trial without model calls at every step.

policy.alt: Hierarchical VLA Design Study policy architecture and execution flow
policy.note: Figure 1: Systematically varies planner, low-level policy, switching, observation and memory interfaces, then instantiates stronger hierarchical robot agents.

policy.alt: RoboClaw policy architecture and execution flow
policy.note: Figure 2: Unifies autonomous collection, policy learning and long-horizon execution under a VLM controller, using forward–inverse skill pairs to reset the workspace.

policy.alt: MimicPlay policy architecture and execution flow
policy.note: Figure 2: Learns latent plans from human play videos and uses them to condition a low-level robot imitation policy for long-horizon manipulation.

policy.alt: SUN Programs / Kuafu policy architecture and execution flow
policy.note: Figure 2: Maintains typed task programs whose grounded relations define aligned control objectives, satisfaction tests and learning rewards throughout policy development.

policy.alt: EXIMO policy architecture and execution flow
policy.note: PDF page 2, Figure 1: VLM-orchestrated exploration produces demonstrations for VLA imitation and residual reinforcement learning.

policy.alt: ST-GPT / SGPT policy architecture and execution flow
policy.note: PDF page 5, Figure 3: subgoal encoder and cross-attention decoder for SGPT action prediction.

policy.alt: Introspective Planning policy architecture and execution flow
policy.note: Figure 1: Retrieves post-hoc explanations of human-approved choices to align robot plan uncertainty with ambiguous instructions and request clarification when needed.

policy.alt: AgentChord policy architecture and execution flow
policy.note: Figure 1: Compiles anticipated failure branches and executable monitors into a task graph so a robot can recover without a fresh high-latency model query.

policy.alt: VoLoAgent policy architecture and execution flow
policy.note: Figure 3: Orchestrates interruptible robot policies and perception tools while monitoring execution and recovering from open-vocabulary manipulation failures.

policy.alt: ICLHF policy architecture and execution flow
policy.note: Figure 2: Uses textual human feedback and physical-constraint feedback to revise a household task plan while a graph-based optimizer grounds spatial relations.

policy.alt: HoloMind / LongAct policy architecture and execution flow
policy.note: Figure 3: two-level planning, executor, spatial / episodic memory and critic feedback in the household agent.

policy.alt: StageGuard policy architecture and execution flow
policy.note: Figure 1: Distills a teacher model’s structured explanations into a compact stage-transition monitor that switches learned robot skills during long-horizon execution.

policy.alt: VA-Bench Shared Agent Harness policy architecture and execution flow
policy.note: Figure 4: Connects general multimodal models to active camera control and metric Cartesian actions, using RGB demonstrations as procedural context.

policy.alt: REVOLVE policy architecture and execution flow
policy.note: Figure 3: Pairs automated geometric reset / correction with external judgment memory and repeated policy updates to improve real manipulation with less manual intervention.

policy.alt: OpenETA policy architecture and execution flow
policy.note: PDF page 2, Figure 1: Places a general reasoning agent above a host-checked tool interface, with fresh visual observations after each world-changing action.

policy.alt: RoboHarness policy architecture and execution flow
policy.note: Figure 1: Routes heterogeneous robot policies using execution memory and prepares their handoffs with memory-derived bridge states.

policy.alt: Robo-Harness K1 policy architecture and execution flow
policy.note: Figure 2: Augments a direct robot-use VLM with calibrated geometry queries, persistent visual anchors and grasp hypotheses while retaining its native tool-call interface.

policy.alt: World Action Agent (WAA) policy architecture and execution flow
policy.note: Figure 2: Lets a VLM rehearse geometric actions, inspect contact views and apply image-space corrections, while reusable skills grow from reviewed experience.

policy.alt: Mimir policy architecture and execution flow
policy.note: PDF page 4, Figure 2: Separates persistent world evidence from task progress, then dynamically grounds the active goal against both memories before acting.

policy.alt: OCC4M policy architecture and execution flow
policy.note: PDF page 2, Figure 1: Tracks object identity and historical locations in a shared frame, then reprojects remembered targets into the current view for a frozen executor.
Figure 1: Keeps persistent episode memory in a reasoning agent and steers one episodically stateless learned action model with text and optional image-space hints.
